source.title: InternVideo2: Scaling Foundation Models for Multimodal Video Understanding
source.authors: Yi Wang; Kunchang Li; Xinhao Li; Jiashuo Yu; Yinan He; Chenting Wang; Guo Chen; Baoqi Pei; Ziang Yan; Rongkun Zheng; Jilan Xu; Zun Wang; Yansong Shi; Tianxiang Jiang; Songze Li; Hongjie Zhang; Yifei Huang; Yu Qiao; Yali Wang; Limin Wang

record.tranche_reason: The paper compares downstream video-task performance across model sizes, bearing on V6, but does not measure pretraining loss or fit scaling laws.
record.gate_note: The paper reports downstream benchmark scores and some 1B-versus-6B comparisons. It does not report held-out cross-entropy loss, power-law fits, loss extrapolation, or compute-optimal parameter/token allocations. Results comparing models without a relevant size comparison, and results solely about other design choices, are not recorded as scaling rows.
record.test_reason: InternVideo2 is a video foundation-model paper. It does not test any version of the language-model scaling-law claim. It reports no held-out pretraining loss, no power-law fit, no extrapolation and no compute-allocation sweep (V1-V5, V7). Its only scale evidence is a two-point comparison of a 1B and a 6B video encoder on downstream benchmarks. That comparison cannot show that performance improves 'predictably' (V6). It is also confounded: the 6B model was trained on more data than the 1B (Table 2: IV-2M vs IV-1.1M; Table 3: IV-400M vs IV-25.5M stage-2 data). The system is also a video encoder, not a language model. The reader's 'tests/T2' on V6 is therefore not accepted, and the size comparison is recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right but incomplete. The authors' main conclusion is that progressive training (masked reconstruction, crossmodal contrastive learning, next-token prediction) and refined video-audio-speech captions give state-of-the-art video understanding. On scale, they say 1B→6B gives notable zero-shot gains (+1.4/+1.9) but marginal finetuned gains (+0.4). They attribute 6B's lower zero-shot Kinetics/UCF/HMDB scores to stage-2 data causing forgetting. They attribute the FineAction non-improvement to scaling capacity without data refinement.
record.recipe_differences: Progressive video-model training and downstream video benchmark evaluation; no language-model held-out-loss scaling-law fitting or compute-optimal allocation procedure.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported effects vary with task and evaluation setting: zero-shot versus finetuning, benchmark dataset, and training stage. The text also notes lower 6B performance than 1B on some zero-shot datasets attributed to the larger model's stage-2 pretraining data.

fits_no_version.finding: Scaling the InternVideo2 video encoder from 1B to 6B, together with more training data, gives small gains on most downstream tasks: +1.4/+1.9 zero-shot averages, gains on grounding and retrieval. Finetuned action recognition gains only +0.4, and FineAction gains little. Zero-shot Kinetics scores fall slightly, which the authors attribute to forgetting after richer stage-2 data.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In video foundation models, a larger encoder trained on more data yields small, task-dependent downstream gains, not uniformly predictable ones.

record.problems: The scaling comparisons generally involve only 1B and 6B models, not a fitted or predictive scaling curve. The reported outcomes are downstream task scores rather than held-out pretraining loss; no uncertainty estimates are stated.
record.rows_left_out: Other benchmark scores and comparisons are not included where the text does not report a size comparison relevant to V6. Some additional scale-related table entries are not included because the reported comparison is not cleanly attributable to model size or is not described as a scaling result in the text.

untested.parts: No held-out pretraining loss or power-law fit in parameters, tokens or compute.
No small-run fit used to predict larger runs.
No fixed-compute allocation of parameters vs tokens.
Video modality, but no loss curve or power-law form is measured.
Only two model sizes with confounded data. No predictive relationship to scale or to pretraining loss, and no language models.
No exponents or fitting choices compared.

missing.what: Further 1B vs 6B downstream comparisons. Linear probing: s1-1B 81.6 vs s1-6B 82.0 on K400. Attentive probing: s2-1B 87.9 vs s2-6B 88.8 on K400. Zero-shot UCF/HMDB/MiT/SSv2-MC/Charades. TAL mAP, including THUMOS 69.8 vs 72.0.
Stage-1 ablation in which ViT-6B with K-Mash2M reaches avg 79.6 vs ViT-1B 79.0. The authors note that MAE data scale must grow with model size or performance saturates.

record.verdict_notes: The 1B and 6B models differ in training data, so size effects are confounded with data. The study concerns video encoders rather than language models and gives no loss or fitted scaling relation. All reader labels are withdrawn. Reference-value rows r1, r3, r5 and r27 should be merged as baselines.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out pretraining loss or power-law relationship in parameters, tokens, or compute is measured.
No small-run fit or prediction of larger-run loss is tested.
No fixed-compute allocation sweep or loss-minimising parameter/token split is tested.
No controlled comparison of depth, width, or other architecture details at fixed parameter count is reported.
The study concerns video models, but does not test whether held-out loss follows a power law in this modality or in other training regimes.

Tests downstream benchmark performance across some model sizes; does not fit a predictive relationship, test prediction from pretraining loss, or establish performance predictability over several orders of magnitude.
No comparison of scaling-law exponents, fitting choices, or departures from a single power law is made.

relation.reason: Discusses scaling model capacity and training data, but neither tests the defined laws nor applies a fitted law as a tool.

tranche.reason: Reports video-model training and downstream comparisons without testing power-law form, extrapolation, compute-optimal allocation, architectural invariance, or quantitative downstream predictability.

source_check.notes: All sampled numerical values, baselines, subjects and conditions match the tables. Effect-state corrections follow the version-relative rules: these rows link to none; model-size comparisons also change training data and establish no predictive scaling law.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Zero-shot video retrieval and temporal grounding comparisons reported in Tables 9 and 11
reader_labels.reason: Most reported size comparisons improve at 6B; see r7-r13, r15-r17, and r19-r26.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Average finetuned action-recognition score and retrieval metrics with small or negative changes
reader_labels.reason: The finetuned action-recognition increase is described as marginal, and some retrieval scores decline slightly; see r6, r14, and r18.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: Zero-shot Kinetics action recognition when comparing InternVideo2clip 1B and 6B
reader_labels.reason: The larger model has lower top-1 or AVG results on the three Kinetics datasets, with no AVG increase on Kinetics-700; see r28-r33.
